_doc: Critic framework. scope selectors: 'all', 'tier:<tier>', 'subtree:<skill-id>' (the skill and all descendants), or a bare skill id. Stages: G1 = framework gauntlet (this phase; every critic reviews the whole framework), G2 = SKILL.md gauntlet (per-skill, scoped), S1 = ADR review, S2 = design/contract review, S3 = implementation review, S4 = validation & release review.

stages.G1: Framework gauntlet: capability map, skill graph, contracts, hierarchy (whole framework)
stages.G2: SKILL.md gauntlet: per-skill description quality, technique currency, validation criteria
stages.S1: ADR review: evidence, alternatives, revisit conditions
stages.S2: Design & contract review: API/contract drafts, data layouts, threading model
stages.S4: Validation & release review: benchmarks, scalability runs, certification readiness

critics.name: Engine Architecture Critic
critics.mandate: Architectural completeness and subsystem boundaries: ownership overlaps, missing contracts, wrong layering, contracts that leak internals, hierarchy that does not match coupling.
checks: every capability has exactly one owner and the owner is the right expertise
non-responsibilities point to the real owner
contracts are minimal, stable and layered
leads have real territory, not just coordination

critics.name: Rendering Critic
critics.mandate: Graphics architecture and currency of rendering techniques; GPU-driven, bindless, explicit-API assumptions; scalability from 2D mobile to path tracing.
checks: no draw-call-centric or DX11-era assumptions on capable tiers; CPU-batched submission on TBDR/lite3d follows RND.ARCH.submission-strategy
render graph owns sync and aliasing
scale-down path exists for each feature

critics.name: Systems Critic
critics.mandate: Concurrency, memory, scheduling, IO and low-level architecture.

critics.name: Physics & Simulation Critic
critics.mandate: Simulation domains: physics, destruction, fluids, cloth, crowds, large-scale simulation, determinism of simulation.
checks: stepping and sync with frame phases are explicit
simulation LOD exists for large scales

critics.name: Networking Critic
critics.mandate: Online and multiplayer architecture: models, replication, prediction, servers, security, online-service boundaries.

critics.name: Tools & Editor Critic
critics.mandate: Production tooling and content workflows: editor, pipeline, collaboration, iteration speed.
checks: large teams can collaborate without lock contention

critics.name: Platform Critic
critics.mandate: Hardware, operating systems, consoles, graphics APIs, packaging and platform requirements.
checks: PAL is the only platform-specific layer
console, mobile and web constraints represented

critics.name: Performance Critic
critics.mandate: Scalability bottlenecks: serialization points, excess synchronization, cache inefficiency, GPU stalls, bandwidth, poor asymptotics.

critics.name: Production Critic
critics.mandate: Could a real team ship games with this: workflows, content scale, team scale, schedules, live operations.
checks: features have an owner through ship

critics.name: Future-Technology Critic
critics.mandate: Does the architecture block likely next-5-year technologies: neural rendering, work graphs, cluster RT, ML animation, new storage and memory, new platforms.
checks: extension points exist for emerging techniques
no hard-coding of today's API limits

critics.name: Completeness Critic
critics.mandate: Exactly one responsibility: find engine capabilities or engineering disciplines that are missing.
checks: compare against shipped engines' feature sets
compare against production pipelines end to end

critics.name: Anti-Legacy Critic
critics.mandate: Find accidental legacy architecture: central sequential update loops, deep inheritance, global state, hot-path virtual dispatch, CPU-driven rendering, coarse locks, global renderer sync, frame-tied lifetimes, universal scene graphs, synchronous IO/loading, single-thread-first design, OpenGL/DX11 assumptions, monoliths. A flagged pattern needs justification, not removal.
checks: each pattern in data/legacy-patterns.json absent or justified by an ADR

critics.name: Game Systems & Content Critic
critics.mandate: Animation, audio, AI, gameplay framework, UI, text, localization and accessibility: whether game teams get what they need.
checks: designers and animators have authoring paths
accessibility and localization built in, not bolted on

critics.name: Testing & Validation Critic
critics.mandate: Validation, oracles, determinism and concurrency testing, agent-output integrity: can an independent critic objectively decide correctness?
checks: each skill has objective validation with an independent oracle

critics.name: Security Critic
critics.mandate: Threat model, trust boundaries, memory safety, supply chain, privacy, incident response — reviewed at design time as well as in code.
checks: every untrusted input has a validating owner and a fuzz target
privacy of telemetry, crash and player data
